steps.say: Identify your purpose, your audience and your text type before you plan.
steps.show: to argue, to inform, to persuade, to entertain

steps.say: Plan your paragraphs, and give each one a clear main idea.
Choose a register that suits your reader: formal for a council, more relaxed for a school magazine.
Use the features of your text type, such as subheadings in an explanation or a flashback in a story.
Edit for clarity and precise words, then proofread for spelling and punctuation.

check.prompt: You want to persuade your town council to build a bicycle lane. Which text should you write?

options.why: A diary is private and is not sent to anyone.
A poem would not set out clear reasons and a request.
Instructions tell someone how to do something.

hints: Think about your purpose and your reader.
A council is an official group, so your writing should be formal.
Which text type can make a request to an official group?
check.explanation: A formal letter is the best way to make a request to an official group such as a town council.
